before.approach: Spire Gully right (Alpenkuhl), part of the Hairpin Crags, is reached from the same large pullout at the hairpin turns on SR-20 near Washington Pass used for Kangaroo Temple. Looking up toward South Early Winter Spire from the pullout, Spire Gully is the obvious gully just below and left; Alpenkuhl is its sunnier, south-facing right side (the left side is known as Tiger Wall). The approach is one of the shortest at Washington Pass — a direct walk/scramble of roughly 10-15 minutes straight up from the highway, snow-covered in early season and a worn boot path later in summer.

_raw.approach: Box Creek Meadows area; Class 2 route to summit via Ice Creek Ridge
_raw.land_manager: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Chelan Ranger District)
_raw.special_features: North face has steep cliffs and glacier remnants; ideal season late Sept-Oct
_raw.fire_restrictions: No fires within 1/2 mile of Ice Lakes, 1/4 mile of Image Lake, or above 4,000 feet on Lime Ridge
_raw.seasonal_closures: NOTE: April 2026 - extreme access limitations due to December 2025 storm damage
_raw.camping_restrictions: No camping within 1/4 mile of Image Lake or 200 feet of Holden/Lyman Lakes
_raw.parking_pass_required: Recreation Pass at trailhead (if developed recreation site)

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.notes: Not inside North Cascades National Park — this corridor is entirely Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District). No Mount Rainier-style climbing fee applies here.
access.rules: No climbing or wilderness permit required for day climbing. Dispersed camping capped at 10 days; no camping within ¼ mile of Cutthroat Lake; no campfires at dispersed sites; bear-resistant food storage required; dogs on leash ≤6 ft.
access.seasonal: WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) closes gate-to-gate roughly early December–mid/late April; the entire Washington Pass corridor is car-inaccessible in winter.
access.landManager: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Chelan Ranger District)
access.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
access.passRequired: Recreation Pass at trailhead (if developed recreation site)

before.watch_out:
Ultra-ephemeral ice formation—even less consistent than Iceman; highly dependent on unusual weather patterns; often forms only in coldest, snowiest years
Water source limited and variable—snowmelt dependency means formation marginal in warm years; verify conditions from recent reports before committing
Highly condition-dependent climbing—ice quality can range from nil to excellent depending on recent weather; check NWAC and recent trip reports before approach
Technical grade masks variable protection—WI3-4 rating assumes quality ice; poor ice conditions create unprotectable runouts with serious consequences
Afternoon deterioration extreme—late morning climbing risky; even slight warming weakens ice; must climb in pre-dawn cold hours only
Significant avalanche exposure in approach—gully terrain subject to slides; assess stability; early start essential for safe approach
Approach terrain variable and sometimes snow-choked—route-finding difficult; terrain traps in gullies; potential for slide; microspikes/crampons needed
Limited climbing window in season—typically Dec-Jan only in most years; highly weather-dependent; low probability of climbable conditions
